messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE — ded-pool 'thundra' node-3 (us-west-2a) reported repeated GPU ECC errors -> driver panic -> host eviction. Observed sudden evict around 2069123430. Several TonicHealth (tenant tonic-prod-3) requests now 500/timeout. Please triage.

ops-maria: taking this. I see health checks flapping and kube evict logs. marking node cordoned.

eng-runtime-lee: on it, looking at runtime logs. initial observation: OOM on GPU driver followed by Xid 13/43 events. Possible firmware/hw fault. Pasting last kernel lines:

```
[2069123429.123] NVRM: Xid (13): PID 14322 GPU:0: Fault at 0x1a3f4 kernel mode, GPU locked
[2069123430.001] kernel: nvidia: gpu 0000:65:00.0: GPU panic - resetting
[2069123430.120] kubelet: evicting pod tonic-infer-5ff7 (container runtime error)
```

eng-runtime-lee: also seeing NVLINK errors in dmesg. nv_peer_mem reports link down intermittently.

infra-raj: can you confirm whether this is spot-backed instance or reserved? I want to know replacement path.

ops-maria: thundra node-3 was a reserved GPU (dedicated) for the pool, not spot. node shows underlying PCIe ECC count rising. Hardware ops needed.

customer-sre-taylor: TonicHealth reports elevated 500s for model endpoint tonic-ccg/v1 since ~2069123445. They are on a 99.9 SLA. We need an ETA for mitigation and a customer-safe workaround.

charlie-oncall: quick mitigation plan: 1) immediate tenant failover to hosted fallback model (if allowed) 2) blacklist node-3 from scheduling / start maintenance workflow 3) kick off hardware replace with HW ops + infra 4) postmortem. Who's owner for 1 and 3?

ops-maria: I will run tenant failover to hosted fallback. Before that, need eng-runtime to ensure model variant mapping exists for tonic-ccg/v1 -> tonic-ccg/v1-hosted (quantized minor diff). If not, we'll route to a compatible smaller variant with cost caveat.

eng-runtime-lee: we have a compatible hosted variant (hosted-ccg-small) but it has 20% throughput impact. I can initiate route override now. Executing route switch via console API.

deploy-bot: deployment triggered: route-override tonic-ccg/v1 -> hosted-ccg-small for tenant tonic-prod-3 by eng-runtime-lee at 2069123460.

eng-runtime-lee: route override applied. Confirming traffic drain from node-3: controller shows connections moving off.

customer-sre-taylor: receiving fewer 500s now, but latency is higher. I'll let TonicHealth know we routed to hosted fallback; share ETA for permanent fix.

support-elaine: drafting customer message: "We detected a GPU hardware fault impacting your dedicated pool instance. We've temporarily routed traffic to a hosted fallback to restore service. Engineers are replacing the faulty node. We'll update within 60 minutes with next steps." Any additions?

charlie-oncall: add that there may be slight increased latency and instance will be replaced; ETA for replacement depends on parts but infra-raj will provide schedule.

infra-raj: starting node replacement. Plan: cordon node -> drain remaining pods -> detach disk -> reprovision new host from pool image -> reattach labels and join cluster. Expected time 25-40 minutes if no parts. Kicking off now.

ops-maria: draining node now: `kubectl drain thundra-node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` output:

```
node/thundra-node-3 cordoned
evicting pod tonic-infer-5ff7
evicting pod tonic-cache-0
unable to evict pod tonic-infer-5ff7: error when evicting pod: cannot delete pod as it is terminating
```

ops-maria: one pod stuck terminating, looks like it's stuck waiting for GPU reset. eng-runtime-lee any tips to force eject?

eng-runtime-lee: you can `kubectl delete pod ... --grace-period=0 --force` as last resort. Also run `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0` on host to attempt reset, but host driver already unstable. If reset fails, container runtime will error. Recommend force delete and let orchestrator reschedule (we already overriding tenant).

ops-maria: doing force delete now.

ops-maria: pod removed. node drained. Moving to reprovision.

infra-raj: reprovision initiated. new instance id i-0f9b3 replacing node-3. Starting image => attaching NVRM firmware X.

eng-runtime-lee: monitoring for nvlink/kernel errors on replacement once it joins. I'll keep an eye on model routing.

deploy-bot: node thundra-node-3 removed from pool, new node thundra-node-7 joined at 2069123580.

ops-maria: new node joined, labels restored. Running smoke test: local `inference-runner` against tonic-ccg/v1 for tenant returns 200s.

customer-sre-taylor: TonicHealth confirms their endpoints are back to normal for the majority of traffic. They still see a handful of retries but no critical impact.

support-elaine: sent update to customer with ETA and explanation. They acknowledged and thanked the team, asked for postmortem link when ready.

charlie-oncall: handoff: eng-runtime-lee will own follow-up diagnostics + postmortem; infra-raj will own hardware ticket and serial trace; ops-maria will verify pool health for next 24h. I'll tag P0 and follow up.

eng-runtime-lee: initial root cause hypothesis: GPU experienced ECC spike leading to driver panic (possible degrading VRAM), non-recoverable on-host. Need to run memtest/firmware check and escalate to vendor if repeated. I'll collect full dmesg, nvml logs, and attach to incident ticket.

infra-raj: opened HW ticket #HW-8721 with vendor, included serial SN and dmesg snippet. ETA vendor ack 2 hours.

charlie-oncall: closing active paging loop. If any regressions, page pageduty. Postmortem assigned to eng-runtime-lee (due in 72h).

oncall-bot: Incident status changed: mitigated -> degraded -> resolved for tenant tonic-prod-3 at 2069123615.

ops-maria: leaving notes in runbook: add extra check for ECC counts > threshold -> auto-route to hosted fallback to reduce customer impact.

eng-runtime-lee: will attach logs and recommended runbook changes to the incident ticket.

customer-sre-taylor: thanks all — I'll keep TonicHealth in the loop and request their SRE to join postmortem if they want.

charlie-oncall: thumbs up :thumbsup: Great job everyone.
